anatomy.intro: The white dots are areoles on a green stem, not attached decorations.

parts.function: The broad green ridge forms part of the photosynthetic stem.
parts.label: Rounded rib

parts.function: The conspicuous woolly cushion carries the tiny spines.
parts.label: White areole

parts.function: Short dark-tipped spines can be easy to overlook among the white wool.
parts.label: Tiny spine

parts.function: A small side shoot repeats the parent’s ribbed body as the plant forms a clump.
parts.label: Basal offset

flowers.text: Large white funnels are borne on tubes around 15–22 cm long. The fragrant display is brief and can extend through the night. Watching an enlarging bud is more useful than expecting a flower on a fixed date.

growth.note: A photographed offset or bud is a useful milestone; neither is guaranteed by a particular birthday.

stages.text: The compact plant shows rounded ribs and scattered white areoles.
stages.title: Single globe

stages.text: Basal shoots may gradually build a cluster around the original body.
stages.title: Widening group

stages.text: Long flower tubes can rise well beyond the small green body.
stages.title: Flowering plant

habitat.text: This familiar horticultural name carries a taxonomic wrinkle: NParks describes Echinopsis subdenudata from Bolivia and Paraguay, while Kew includes it within Echinopsis ancistrophora and gives that accepted species a northwestern Argentine range. These are different treatments, not evidence of this nursery plant’s exact origin. The collection retains its recognizable labeled name.

image.alt: Domino cactus with numbered rounded rib, white woolly areole, tiny dark spine and basal offset.

lookalikes.name: Astrophytum asterias
lookalikes.text: Both can look like nearly spineless dotted globes. NParks distinguishes the domino cactus’s more sharply separated ribs from the broad, flatter ribs of A. asterias.

mature.text: The horticultural subdenudata form stays compact: LLIFLE describes individual bodies around 7–12 cm across, with clumps becoming wider through offsets. A collection plant need not reach the dimensions of every form included under ancistrophora.

milestones.text: Joined the collection from Costa Farms.
milestones.title: Acquired

nameStory.text: Subdenudata remains useful on nursery labels even though Kew treats it as a synonym. Keeping both names visible makes the plant easier to recognize across horticultural and taxonomic references.
